sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5.93 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
The shape is a decelerating ramp: growth ran 104.0% in FY2017 and 64.2% in FY2021, then 0.1% in FY2023 and 10.6% in FY2025 [D36][D218][D311][D406].
The FY2017 operating loss of $3.49 billion was driven by a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation, primarily the CEO award and IPO-related RSUs [F12][P74].
The FY2022 reversal, with the operating loss widening 98.7% to $1.40 billion, came from higher cost of revenue and operating expenses, partly offset by revenue [F17][D264][P42].
North America remains the largest driver at 58.6% of FY2025 revenue, contributing 4.4pp of the 10.6% growth [D456][D458][D406].
Other Revenue contributed 5.4pp in FY2025 on 62.9% growth, lifting its share to 12.6% from 4.3% in FY2023 [D545][D544][D543][D539].
Advertising revenue rose $282.4 million on roughly 17% more impressions, partly offset by a 10% lower cost per impression, while other revenue gained $287.6 million on subscriber growth [P24].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth, so revenue grew 5.5pp faster than operating costs [D423][D406][D430].
The operating loss narrowed 32.4% to $532.2 million while the diluted share count rose 2.1%, so the per-share loss fell 35.7% [D407][F20][D425][D410].
The FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is the window high, above the -32.4% median and far above the -422.5% low [F30][D554][D555][D553].
The 5.7pp improvement came from cost of revenue (+1.1pp), R&D (+1.3pp) and other lines (+3.3pp) [D419][D431][D432][D433].
The R&D line rose $101.9 million on product development and headcount, partly offset by $38.8 million of prior-year restructuring charges [P23].
In FY2025 net margin of -7.8% sat 1.2pp above the -9.0% operating margin, helped by $68.9 million of other income [F50][F30][D591][X130].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million exceeded the $460.5 million net loss in FY2025, and free cash flow reached $437.2 million, a 7.4% margin [F80][F40][F100][D393].
Operating cash flow rose from $413.5 million, driven by non-cash stock-based compensation of $1.0 billion and D&A of $163.6 million [P13].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A [F90][D392][D395].
Capex in both years was primarily improvements to leased facilities to support team workspaces [P10].
Net cash turned to net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025, or -10.1% of revenue, against a 45.0% peer median and the 0th percentile of five internet peers [D399][D400][D579][D578].
The February 2025 repurchases of $1.4 billion of notes were funded by $1.47 billion of net proceeds from the 2033 Notes [P1][P2].
Buybacks of $750.9 million were 171.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count still rose 2.1% [X156][D402][D425].
The current ratio of 3.56x is the window low, below the 5.15x median [F180][D565][D567].
Net losses have persisted for ten straight years, from $514.6 million in FY2016 to $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
The loss is narrowing but the company still has not earned a profit in any year of the window [R1].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last nine years [R2][D390].
At 191.1% of the operating loss, compensation is the main reason the GAAP loss persists [R2][D404].
Net cash fell for four years into net debt, reaching -$596.3 million in FY2025 [R3][D399].
Debt-funded buybacks while loss-making leave less cushion than the peer median [R3][R4].
Whether the FY2026 operating margin holds above the -9.0% FY2025 level, in the FY2026 10-K [F30].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue stays below the -10.1% FY2025 level or returns toward zero, in the FY2026 10-K [D400].
Whether stock-based compensation falls below the 17.1% of revenue recorded in FY2025, in the FY2026 10-K [D390].
